summary.title: llvm-mca - LLVM Machine Code Analyzer
summary.one_liner: llvm-mca statically estimates throughput (IPC, Block RThroughput) and per-resource pressure for assembly code on a CPU whose LLVM scheduling model exists, and shows how to read its reports and timeline view.
takeaways: llvm-mca takes assembly (piped from clang or read from a file) and simulates it over a loop of iterations (default 100) to estimate IPC and resource usage for a chosen -mcpu.
The first report section gives IPC, uOps per cycle, DispatchWidth and Block RThroughput; lower Block RThroughput is better.
The resource pressure view shows how cycles are spread across processor resource units; pressure concentrated on a few resources signals a bottleneck.
The timeline view (-timeline) shows each instruction's dispatch, execute, and retire states per cycle, plus average wait times.
Code regions can be selected with LLVM-MCA-BEGIN/LLVM-MCA-END comments, and LLVM-MCA-LATENCY can override instruction latencies, e.g. to model cache misses.
summary.summary: The page is the official LLVM command guide for llvm-mca, a tool that statically measures machine code performance using LLVM scheduling models for a specific CPU. It documents usage examples (piping clang assembly output), the full option list (mcpu, iterations, timeline, resource-pressure, bottleneck-analysis, json and more), and region markers for analyzing specific code blocks. It explains how the tool works and walks through a dot-product example report, covering the summary metrics, instruction info, resource pressure, and timeline view. The accuracy of its results depends on the quality of the backend scheduling models.
